title: Quarter-Wave Initialized 36-Layer Stack with Bounded Gradient Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: A 36-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 alternating stack initialized at quarter-wave optical thickness centered on 560 nm passband, with thickness bounds shifted to 30-340 nm away from singular edges, will achieve better numerical convergence than pure random initialization while maintaining dual-stopband suppression capability.
design_principle: Modified quarter-wavelength optimization: start with λ/4n layers at passband center (560 nm), then vary optical thickness through bounded gradient optimization to smooth spectral characteristics and broaden suppression bands at 355-365 nm and 1030-1080 nm.
proposed_topology: Air | (Ta2O5 | SiO2) × 18 pairs | Fused Silica substrate. Total 36 finite layers, alternating high-low index sequence starting with Ta2O5.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses (36 variables, bounded 30-340 nm)
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds 30-340 nm avoid deposition singularities near 20/350 nm edges
Ta2O5/SiO2 material pair compatible with standard deposition techniques
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflection bands
Transfer-matrix method for coherent planar multilayer interference
Bounded optimization for thickness variables within manufacturing constraints
expected_advantages: Quarter-wave initialization provides physically meaningful starting point
Shifted thickness bounds (30-340 nm) reduce numerical singularities
Gradient optimization can refine from good initial guess
known_risks: May converge to local minimum near quarter-wave solution
36 layers may still cause numerical conditioning issues
Dual-stopband requirement may conflict with single quarter-wave center
execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 36-layer planar dielectric filter on fused silica substrate. Stack topology: Air incident medium | Ta2O5(1) | SiO2(2) | Ta2O5(3) | SiO2(4) | Ta2O5(5) | SiO2(6) | Ta2O5(7) | SiO2(8) | Ta2O5(9) | SiO2(10) | Ta2O5(11) | SiO2(12) | Ta2O5(13) | SiO2(14) | Ta2O5(15) | SiO2(16) | Ta2O5(17) | SiO2(18) | Ta2O5(19) | SiO2(20) | Ta2O5(21) | SiO2(22) | Ta2O5(23) | SiO2(24) | Ta2O5(25) | SiO2(26) | Ta2O5(27) | SiO2(28) | Ta2O5(29) | SiO2(30) | Ta2O5(31) | SiO2(32) | Ta2O5(33) | SiO2(34) | Ta2O5(35) | SiO2(36) | Fused Silica substrate. All 36 layers have individual thickness optimization variables bounded 30-340 nm. Initialize thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness: Ta2O5 layers at 560 nm/(4*n_Ta2O5), SiO2 layers at 560 nm/(4*n_SiO2). Illumination: 0 degree incidence, unpolarized light. Simulation wavelength grid must cover 350-1100 nm with sufficient resolution to evaluate target bands: 355 nm (single wavelength), 355-365 nm (band), 420-700 nm (passband), 1030-1080 nm (band). Optimize using gradient-based method to maximize passband transmittance while minimizing stopband transmittance. Report thicknesses_nm for all 36 layers, best_target_score, valid_candidates count, and tightest_margin. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization unpolarized. wavelength intervals 355-355 nm, 355-365 nm, 420-700 nm, 1030-1080 nm. soft objectives: high average transmittance in 420-700 nm; low average transmittance at 355 nm; low average transmittance in 355-365 nm; low average transmittance in 1030-1080 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance at 355 nm; high transmittance in 355-365 nm; high transmittance in 1030-1080 nm; high loss in 420-700 nm. manufacturing constraints: maximum 36 layers; layer thickness range 20-350 nm.
revision_reason: Repair compilation failure from iteration_06 (target band grid overlap error) by ensuring wavelength grid covers all target bands. Address numerical_convergence from iteration_02 by using quarter-wave initialization and shifted thickness bounds (30-340 nm instead of 20-350 nm) to avoid edge singularities.
